name: adapter_health
description: Use when readings drop out, the app keeps disconnecting or data looks odd, to rule the OBD adapter in or out before blaming the car.
instructions: Call check_adapter {} once: it reads the adapter firmware, the supply voltage it sees and the protocol, then times 5 requests and grades the adapter good, ok or poor.
Read the grade first, then the latency and timeouts; mention the firmware only when it is flagged as a clone or missing.
This checks the adapter, not the car: never turn a poor adapter grade into a vehicle fault.
interpret: Grade good: the adapter answers quickly; dropouts are then more likely the car, the wiring or the phone's Bluetooth link.
Grade ok: usable; a clone firmware string (v1.5, v2.1) caps an otherwise fast adapter at ok, and it may show occasional protocol quirks.
Grade poor: slow (median over 150 ms on CAN, over 400 ms on K-line) or not answering; advise reseating the adapter or trying a better one before trusting live data.
Timeouts above 0 of 5 mean requests went unanswered: with a good median that points to an intermittent link, not a slow adapter.

The voltage is the car's supply at the OBD socket as the adapter reads it: under 11.5 V with the engine off is a weak battery or ignition off, and live readings may drop out. With the engine running, a voltage under 13.5 V = not charging.
